chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked: 'Are the two rak'ahs of Fajr part of the night prayer?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَا الْفَجْرِ: The two rak'ahs of the dawn/Fajr prayer

ai.seo_question: Are the two rak'ahs of Fajr considered part of the night prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the two voluntary rak'ahs of Fajr are explicitly identified as part of *Salat al-Layl* (night prayer), a classification that underscores their spiritual significance as a continuation of the night vigil. This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing these specific units from the obligatory Fajr prayer and linking them to the broader tradition of night worship emphasized by the Ahl al-Bayt.
